author: Vincent Augerot
name: HardSlice aggregate
description: An aggregate of a module of a hardslice-api solution: its root, its typed identifier, its EF Core mapping in the module and its unit tests. Run it from the root of the solution with --project src/<App>/<App>.csproj.

Module.description: The module of the aggregate, in PascalCase, such as Rooms: src/<App>/Features/<Module>/<Module>Module.cs must exist.

Table.description: The table of the aggregate: letters, digits and underscores, such as Categories. The name of the aggregate followed by s by default.

postActions.description: The migration to add and the aggregate to complete.

manualInstructions.text:
Complete the aggregate AggregateName of module ModuleName, then add its migration:
1. Give AggregateName its state and its rules in src/MyApp.Domain/ModuleName/AggregateName.cs: name its factory method Create after the business fact, take the state of the new aggregate as parameters and throw a DomainException for each rule they break. Map that state in src/MyApp/Features/ModuleName/AggregateNameConfiguration.cs, which AppDbContext applies by itself: there is nothing to register.
2. Replace the TODO(hardslice): marker of tests/MyApp.Tests/Domain/ModuleName/AggregateNameTests.cs: the check fails while it is left.
3. Add the migration of the table AggregateTable from the root of the solution, once the mapping is complete:
dotnet tool restore
dotnet ef migrations add AddAggregateTable --project src/MyApp --output-dir Shared/Persistence/Migrations
Until it exists, the integration tests fail the check: MigrationsTests finds changes missing from the migrations, and once the solution has a migration, EF Core refuses to migrate the database of the others.
